name_reason: Already matches fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> (domain=battle/inventory helper). Descriptor accurately reflects 'find the equipped inventory slot filtered by item kind'. No address residue; trailing tokens (by_kind) are semantic words, not hex. Verified accurate against decompile and all 8 callers.
purpose: Scan a combatant's 8 inventory slots and return the index of the first slot that is equipped (flag bit6/0x40) and whose item_id falls in the requested kind range (physical <0x80 vs magical >=0x80); -1 if none.
logic_summary: Loops slot_iter 0..7 over data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr[char_idx].inventory_slots[] (16-byte array at runtime_char +0x0A = 8 two-byte slots: [0]=flag, [1]=item_id; 80-byte runtime_char stride). Match condition: (flag & 0x40)!=0 AND ((kind==0 && item_id<0x80) || (kind!=0 && item_id>=0x80)). Returns first matching slot_iter, else 0xFFFFFFFF. The 0x80 cut is the physical(0x00..0x7F)/magical(0x80..0xD6) item split per assets/items.md. Leading __CHK(0xC,...) is the Watcom stack/bounds-check CRT intrinsic, not game logic.

params.name: param_1
params.semantics: Index into the runtime_char array (which combatant). Used as data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr[param_1]. Callers pass attacker/defender/caster/char unit indices. src already names this char_idx.
params.reason: Live Ghidra name param_1 is a generic placeholder carrying no semantics; char_idx matches the src declaration and the runtime_char-array index usage. Rename recorded only; applied in Stage 2.

params.name: param_2
params.semantics: Item-kind selector controlling the item_id range branch: 0 = physical (item_id<0x80, weapon/armor); non-zero = magical (item_id>=0x80, spellbook/magic item). src already names this kind. All 8 current callers pass 0.
params.reason: Live Ghidra name param_2 is a generic placeholder; kind matches the src declaration and the selector usage (chooses the <0x80 vs >=0x80 branch). Rename recorded only; applied in Stage 2.

returns.semantics: Index (0..7) of the first matching equipped inventory slot, or 0xFFFFFFFF (-1) when no equipped slot matches the requested kind. Callers typically feed the slot to fd2_get_inventory_slot_item_id, and treat 0xFFFFFFFF as 'no weapon equipped' (disable attack / cannot counter / -1 hit-rate).

comment_original_issue: src comment was accurate and concise on the algorithm and the 0x80 split, but did not note that every current caller passes kind=0 (so the kind!=0 / >=0x80 branch is presently unexercised); added one clarifying sentence.
notes: All 8 callers (fd2_ai_score_physical_attack, fd2_animate_attack_hit_sequence, fd2_animate_combat_hit_with_hp_drain, fd2_calculate_combat_hit_outcome, fd2_check_can_counter_attack, fd2_check_can_default_attack_target, fd2_execute_attack_damage_calculation, fd2_player_inline_action_menu_dispatch) pass kind=0 -> always the weapon/physical (<0x80) path. The kind!=0 (>=0x80) branch exists in the binary but is unused; the menu's spell-slot gating uses fd2_build_usable_spell_list, not this function. Ghidra plate previously claimed kind=1 is used for spell prerequisite/menu checks -- contradicted by call-site evidence, so plate 'usage' section was corrected to match. src represents the 2-byte slot layout as a flat byte array (inventory_slots[slot*2], [slot*2+1]); Ghidra views it as a struct array (pInventory_slots[slot].bSlot_flag/.bItem_id) -- equivalent. struct types.h: runtime_char +0x0A inventory_slots[16]. item 0x80=布衣 etc confirm 0x80+ range includes armor/consumables too, so the magical label is the binary's coarse split rather than strictly spellbooks; behavior is purely the numeric 0x80 cut. No logic issues.
